The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(v_p(n)\) denote the exponent of a prime \(p\) in \(n\).

A move replacing \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) replaces each pair of exponents \((v_p(a),v_p(b))\) by \((\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b)))\). Thus, for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

A move changes the board exactly when the two chosen numbers are not comparable by divisibility. When Mark stops, every pair on the board is comparable by divisibility, so the final numbers form a chain under divisibility.

Since each prime’s exponent multiset is invariant, the final sorted list is forced: if the final numbers sorted increasingly are \(x_1\le x_2\le\cdots\le x_{2100}\), then for every prime \(p\), the sequence
\[
v_p(x_1)\le v_p(x_2)\le\cdots\le v_p(x_{2100})
\]
is exactly the sorted list of the exponents among \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

We need the \(2026\)th smallest final number. Equivalently, for each prime \(p\), we need the \(2026\)th smallest value of \(v_p(n)\) for \(1\le n\le 2100\). This is the same as the
\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]
th largest value of \(v_p(n)\).

The \(75\)th largest \(p\)-adic exponent is the largest \(t\ge 0\) such that at least \(75\) of the numbers \(1,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^t\). The number of such multiples is \(\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor\). Hence the exponent of \(p\) in the desired number is
\[
e_p=\max\left\{t\ge 0:\left\lfloor\frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor\ge 75\right\}.
\]
Since
\[
\frac{2100}{75}=28,
\]
this condition is equivalent to
\[
p^t\le 28.
\]

Now list the primes and their corresponding exponents:

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
p & 2 & 3 & 5 & 7 & 11 & 13 & 17 & 19 & 23\\
\hline
e_p & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1
\end{array}
\]

For all other primes, \(e_p=0\). Therefore the \(2026\)th smallest final number is
\[
2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2^6
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
